prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: Robotic solar installation exists only at pilot and early commercial scale, far from the Main KPI of 1,000,000 MW installed by robots per year (more than all solar installed worldwide: about 647-698 GW in 2025, https://www.pv-tech.org/global-solar-pv-installations-reached-647gw-in-2025/). The leading robots still work with human crews: AES Maximo installed 100 MW at Bellefield by March 2026 (https://www.pv-tech.org/youre-going-to-see-a-lot-more-of-these-maximo-on-robotic-installation-utility-scale-solar-projects/); Terabase Terafab V2 finished field testing in 2026 with a rated output of about 1 GW per line-year and autonomous rovers still promised (https://www.terabase.energy/resources/terabase-energys-next-generation-terafab-completes-field-testing-ready-for-deployment); Built Robotics' autonomous pile driver runs with a two-person crew (https://www.builtrobotics.com/press/the-elusive-dream-of-fully-autonomous-construction-vehicles). No open-source end-to-end crewless system was found; Luminous has announced an open construction dataset only. Honest limit: module pick-and-place, autonomous piling and field-factory assembly are commercial prior art; tasks must target the unsolved parts (crewless site prep, trenching, electrical termination, QA, and generalising across terrain) with their own prior-art basis.
